Woe (ويل) is a word denoting punishment, or it is a valley in Hell. ﴿Woe to those who give less than due﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 2:

﴿Those who, when they take a measure from [the] people, take it in full.﴾ That is, "from" (أيْ مِن, ay min) ﴿the people﴾, ﴿they take in full﴾ the measure.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 83, verse 3:

﴿And when they measure for them⦅i.e., they measure out for them⦆ or weigh for them⦅i.e., they weigh out for them⦆, they cause loss⦅they give less than due in the measure or the weight⦆.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 4:

﴿Alā﴾ is an interrogative of reproach (istifhām tawbīkh). ﴿Yaẓunnu﴾ means yatayaqqan (is certain). "Ulā'ika annahum mab'ūthūn" (Do they not think that they will be resurrected?—that is, they are certain that they will be resurrected).
﴿For a Great Day﴾ — i.e., in it, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿The Day﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, a word that replaces another in its grammatical position) for the place (*mahall*) of "*li-yawmin*" (for a Day). Its governing word (*nasib*) is "*mab'uthun*" (they will be resurrected). ﴿When mankind stands﴾ from their graves ﴿before the Lord of the worlds﴾, the creation, for the sake of His command, His reckoning and His recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 7:

﴿Nay!﴾ Truly, ﴿the record of the wicked﴾ i.e., the record of the deeds of the disbelievers ﴿is in Sijjin﴾. It has been said that it is a register comprehensive of the deeds of the devils and the disbelievers. It has also been said that it is a place at the lowest part of the seventh earth, and it is the abode of Iblis and his armies.
﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ It is a register (kitab) of Sijjin.
﴿A written record﴾ sealed.
﴿Those who deny the Day of Recompense﴾. Al-Jaza' (the Recompense) is a badal (substitute, in grammatical terms an apposition) or a bayan (clarifying apposition) for al-mukadhdhibin (those who deny).
And none deny it except every transgressor (mu'tadi), one who exceeds the limit, sinful (athim), an intensive form (sigha mubalagha).

﴿When Our verses are recited to him﴾ (the Qur'an), ﴿he says, "Tales of the ancients."﴾ (the stories that were written down long ago). It is the plural of أُسْطُورَة (usṭūra), with a damma, or إسْطارَة (isṭāra), with a kasra.
﴿Nay﴾ is a rebuke and a deterrence for their saying that. ﴿Rather, there has settled over﴾ (prevailed over) ﴿their hearts﴾ and covered them, ﴿what they used to earn﴾ of sins. It is like rust.
Nay, [it is] true: ﴿Indeed, they, from their Lord, that Day﴾, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will surely be veiled﴾, so they will not see Him.

Then indeed they will surely burn in the Blazing Fire.

Note: The passage given to me is Tafsir al-Jalalayn's gloss on the verse, which reads: "Then indeed they will surely enter the scorching Fire."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 17:

﴿Then it will be said﴾ to them, ﴿This is﴾ i.e., the punishment "that which you used to deny."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 18:

﴿Kallā﴾ (Indeed, not so), in truth, ﴿indeed the record of the righteous﴾, i.e., the record of the deeds of the believers who are truthful in their faith, ﴿is in ʿIlliyyūn﴾. It has been said that it is a book comprehensive of the deeds of goodness, [recorded] by the angels and the believers of the two species (humans and jinn). It has also been said that it is a place in the seventh heaven, beneath the Throne.
﴿And what will make you know what is ʿIlliyyun?﴾ (It means) it informs you of what ʿIlliyyun is. ﴿It is a register,﴾ meaning the book of ʿIlliyyin.
﴿A written record﴾ sealed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 21:

﴿Witnessed by those brought near (to Allah)﴾ from among the angels.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 22:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾ [i.e., in] Paradise.

On the couches they will gaze (ﷻ) — "On the couches" (al-arā'ik): the thrones (al-surur) within the canopies (al-hijāl). "They will gaze" (yanẓurūna): at what they have been given of bounty (al-ni'īm).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 24:

﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾ (the brightness of enjoyment and its beauty)
﴿They will be given to drink of a pure wine (raḥīq)﴾ — wine (khamr) unmixed with impurity — ﴿sealed﴾ on its vessel, which none but they will be able to break open.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 26:

﴿Its seal is musk﴾, i.e., the last of its drink will be fragrant with the smell of musk. ﴿And for that let those who strive, strive﴾, i.e., let them be eager, hastening to obedience to God.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 83, verse 27:**

﴿And its mixture﴾, i.e., that with which it is mixed, ﴿is from Tasnim﴾, which is explained by His words "عَيْنًا" (a spring).

[The word] ﴿a spring﴾ is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb, *amdaḥa* (أمدح, "I praise [it] most"), ﴿from which those brought near will drink﴾, meaning "from it." Or *yashrab* (يشرب, "drinks") is construed to include the meaning of *yaltadhdhu* (يلتذ, "takes delight in"), [so that the preposition *bi-* is used].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 29:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾ such as Abu Jahl and the like, ﴿used to laugh at those who believed﴾ such as ʿAmmar and Bilal and the like, ﴿mocking them﴾.
﴿And when they passed by them﴾, that is, the believers, ﴿they winked at one another﴾. The criminals gestured to the believers with their eyelids and eyebrows, mocking them.

﴿And when they returned﴾, meaning went back, ﴿to their people, they returned jesting﴾. And in another recitation (qira'a), فَكِهِينَ, meaning delighted (معجبين), mocking the believers by mentioning them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 32:

﴿And when they saw them﴾, i.e., the believers, ﴿they said, "Indeed, these are misguided"﴾ because of their faith in Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 83, verse 33:

﴿And they had not been sent﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿as guardians over them﴾ over the believers, ﴿to watch over them﴾ either over them or over their deeds, ﴿so that they might lead them to their interests﴾

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 83 (al-Mutaffifin), verse 34:

"﴿So today﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection, [it is] those who believed, from among the disbelievers, who laugh."
On the couches (in Paradise), they gaze (from their dwellings) at the disbelievers while they are being punished, and they laugh at them, just as the disbelievers laughed at them in the world.
﴿Will the disbelievers be recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ — was recompensed. ﴿Yes.﴾
